premises.statement: Every project entering the health-indicator calculation has at least one completed task.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: quality_tasks/NULLIF(completed_tasks,0) ... quality_percentage BETWEEN 0 AND 100 ... FROM final WHERE is_valid_record
premises.alternative: The contract says percentages must be set to 0 "when denominator is 0"; the final SELECT applies COALESCE only after the validity filter has excluded rows with null percentages.
premises.reason: Projects with no completed tasks, including projects with no tasks, would be excluded instead of receiving the specified zero percentages.

premises.statement: The last 12 months of productivity output means the current calendar month plus the preceding 11 calendar months.
premises.alternative: The contract says "activity_month within the last 12 months", which could instead mean a cutoff at CURRENT_DATE minus 12 months.
premises.reason: The interpretation determines whether an additional boundary month appears in the output.

premises.statement: A timezone-naive month bucket satisfies the productivity model's timezone-aware activity_month requirement.
premises.alternative: Staging declares created_at as "TIMESTAMP", while activity_month is declared "TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE" with the description "timezone preserved".
premises.reason: The expression inherits a timezone-naive staging type rather than establishing the required output type.

premises.statement: The 24-month productivity computation window starts exactly 24 months before the current date rather than at a calendar-month boundary.
premises.alternative: The contract describes "Monthly user productivity trends" using a "24-month history", which also permits a calendar-month-aligned interpretation.
premises.reason: A partially included earliest month can change cumulative totals and historical window calculations.

premises.statement: No tasks included in the productivity calculation have future creation timestamps.
premises.alternative: The contract limits aggregation to tasks "created in the last 24 months" and output to "the last 12 months"; neither filter supplies an upper bound.
premises.reason: Future-dated tasks could introduce future reporting months and alter cumulative metrics.

premises.statement: Project deadline status should compare only the calendar date of project_due_date with today.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: WHEN project_due_date::DATE>CURRENT_DATE THEN 'on_time' WHEN project_due_date::DATE=CURRENT_DATE THEN 'due_today'
premises.alternative: The contract defines due_date as TIMESTAMP and says "on_time if due_date > today; due_today if equal", which could instead require direct timestamp comparison.
premises.reason: Projects due later today can receive different deadline and forecast labels under the two interpretations.

premises.statement: Task creation and completion timestamps used for project recency counts are never in the future.
premises.alternative: The contract requires tasks created or completed "within the last 7 days", whereas these conditions have no upper bound.
premises.reason: Future timestamps would inflate recent activity counts and activity_percentage.

premises.statement: Every retained project's creation calendar date is on or before the current date.
premises.alternative: The contract describes project_age_days as a "non-negative integer", but the calculation and validity checks do not enforce that bound.
premises.reason: Future-dated projects would produce negative ages contrary to the declared output constraint.

fewer.reason: Four distinct unestablished premises were identifiable; the remaining logic largely implements explicit contract rules or relies on staging guarantees already covered by earlier reviews.
